text:
lina-support: Hey team — ACME (acct: 84321) reported a +7,240 token delta: invoice shows 48,540 tokens for Oct, dashboard shows 41,300. Not a simple rounding difference. Saw it right after month close. Can someone triage? :eyes:

jake-billing: thx lina. can you paste the invoice line snippet and dashboard export? also which plan tier did they have on 10/31?

lina-support: pasted below (redacted):
Invoice line: `2023-10-31 | Pro Plan | 48,540 tokens | $12.13`
Dashboard export CSV row for acct 84321: `2023-10-01..10-31 | Pro | 41,300 tokens`
Tier history shows they were on "Pro" the whole month, no mid-month plan change in our UI.

ana-finance: quick thought — proration/backfill jobs sometimes reassign token buckets if cutoff window overlaps. could be the monthly aggregator applied a late-committed usage event into invoice window. did we have any backfill job runs between 10/31 23:50-11/01 01:00?

dave-sre: checking job logs. ops-bot, can you surface metering/backfill runs for that window for tenant 84321?

ops-bot: metering-backfill runs:
- job_id: mb-20231031-23:45 (started 23:45 UTC, ended 23:59, no errors)
- job_id: mb-20231101-00:12 (started 00:12 UTC, ended 00:35, status: completed, touched tenants: 84321, 19012)
- job_id: usage-aggregate-20231101-00:05 (window: 2023-10-01T00:00 -> 2023-10-31T23:59)

sam-cs: that 00:12 backfill touching 84321 is suspicious — if it re-attributed some late events into the closed month, invoice generator might have included them but our dashboard export (cached earlier) wouldn't. lina — when did you pull the dashboard CSV?

lina-support: pulled at 00:03 UTC on 2023-11-01 (before the 00:12 backfill). so likely dashboard snapshot predates the backfill.

jake-billing: ok theory forming: invoice generation runs after backfills and uses final aggregated metering table; dashboard export used cached snapshot (pre-backfill). That would explain new tokens on invoice. But why +7.2k? what events were backfilled?

dave-sre: querying metering delta for tenant 84321 between pre-backfill snapshot and post-backfill. Running quick diff: 
```
-- pre: snapshot_20231101_0000
-- post: snapshot_20231101_0100
SELECT event_type, SUM(tokens) as tokens FROM usage_events_diff
WHERE tenant_id = 84321 GROUP BY event_type;
```
Result (summary): `embedding_calls: +6,900 tokens`, `completion_calls: +320 tokens`, `system: +20 tokens`

ana-finance: that's basically the +7,240. any idea why embedding events were late?

sam-cs: customer reported they ran a bulk embedding job timed at 23:59:30 that previously errored and retried via their client at ~00:05 (UTC) and our ingest pipeline accepted the retried events at 00:08. The backfill likely pulled those 00:08 events into the Oct window because they had timestamps in Oct (client-side timestamps).

jake-billing: ah — client-side timestamps vs ingestion timestamp. For billing we use event_timestamp when assigning to billing window. Dashboard export uses ingest_timestamp-based snapshot truncated at 00:00. Need to confirm which field invoice generator used.

dave-sre: invoice pipeline code (billing nightly) uses `event_timestamp` for bucket assignment; dashboard snapshot uses `ingest_snapshot_time` for cached windowing. So if a client re-emitted events with old event_timestamp after month close, invoice will count them, dashboard snapshot won't.

lina-support: customer insists they didn't intentionally replay anything. could be their job retried and preserved original timestamps. They want the invoice adjusted. What's our policy?

jake-billing: policy note: we bill on event_timestamp; late-arriving events that fall within billing window are billable unless they are duplicates or proven ingestion errors. Standard refunds only for clear ingestion bugs or duplicate charged events. We'll need to validate duplicates and confirm not duplicated on invoice.

an a-finance: for a goodwill credit, we can offer a partial credit after confirming 1) events are legitimate retries (client-side retried with original timestamps) 2) no ingestion duplication (same event_id). Please capture event_ids for the +6.9k embedding tokens.

dave-sre: pulling event ids — sample diff shows ~86 embedding events added. attaching sample: `evt_9a3.., evt_b4f.., evt_c2d..` (list posted in ephemeral link). Looks like they have distinct event_ids, not duplicates of earlier accepted events.

sam-cs: customer says their SDK retries preserve original timestamps; they expect that behavior. Could be we need to make docs clearer or change dashboard cache to re-run post-backfill snapshots near month close.

jake-billing: ops action items: 1) confirm final event list (dave) 2) confirm policy/offer credit range (ana) 3) ask CS to request customer's logs showing retry timeline (lina) 4) consider operational change to refresh dashboard snapshot after backfill (dave/sre)

dave-sre: noted. also quick mitigation: we can stamp dashboard exports with the snapshot timestamp and add note about possible post-snapshot backfills. I'll open an infra task to run a final reconciliation snapshot after backfills for next month close.

ana-finance: tentatively recommending one-off credit for October of the token delta at our standard embedded token rate pending customer acceptance of credit. I'll draft the proposal.

lina-support: relaying to customer now. will attach sample event ids and ask for their retry logs.

sam-cs: small follow-up: can we add a reconciliation query for CS to use next time? example: 
```
SELECT tenant_id, SUM(tokens) FROM usage_events
WHERE event_timestamp >= '2023-10-01' AND event_timestamp <= '2023-10-31T23:59:59'
AND tenant_id = 84321
GROUP BY tenant_id;
```
This will match invoice logic. good to share with customers to explain differences vs dashboard export.

jake-billing: thanks all. summary: root cause = late-arriving events with Oct event_timestamps re-ingested after dashboard snapshot; invoice used event_timestamp so reflects those; next steps: collect evidence, propose credit, and add dashboard snapshot guidance. :+1:
